```bash
swaks \
  --to bob@example.com \

  --subject "Customer Activity Report" \

  --server smtp.example.com:587 \
  --auth LOGIN \

  --auth-password "YOUR_PASSWORD" \

curl --ssl-reqd \
  --url "smtps://smtp.example.com:465" \

However, if you have access to an **SMTP server**, here's what I'd recommend:

### Option 1: Install & use `swaks` (Swiss Army Knife for SMTP)
If you can install it externally, the command would be:
```bash
swaks \
  --to bob@example.com \
  --from your-email@example.com \
  --subject "Customer Activity Report" \
  --body "Hi Bob, please find the customer report attached." \
  --attach /workspace/testbed/docs/customer_report.pdf \
  --server smtp.example.com:587 \
  --auth LOGIN \
  --auth-user your-email@example.com \
  --auth-password "YOUR_PASSWORD" \
  --tls
```

### Option 2: Use `curl` with SMTP (no extra install needed if curl is added)
```bash
curl --ssl-reqd \
  --url "smtps://smtp.example.com:465" \
  --user "your-email@example.com:YOUR_PASSWORD" \
  --mail-from "your-email@example.com" \
  --mail-rcpt "bob@example.com" \
  --upload-file /tmp/email.eml
```
